handbook.bettercoppers.title: Golem Handbook
handbook.bettercoppers.welcome.title: Welcome
handbook.bettercoppers.welcome.text:
Copper golems in this mod are small, slightly clumsy workers. Give one a job item and a home chest, and it sorts, mines, farms, fishes or carries goods for you.

# Your first golem
Put a carved pumpkin on a copper block. The golem appears, and the copper block turns into a copper chest: that chest can be its home.

# Three steps
1. Sneak + right-click the golem with a job item.
2. Sneak + right-click it with an empty hand. It glows and shows its status.
3. Right-click its copper chest (within 32 blocks). That is now its home.

Everything you give a golem takes sneak + right-click. A plain click never takes anything from a golem with a job.

# The guide
Open your advancements (L). The Better Coppers tab leads you through everything, one step at a time.
handbook.bettercoppers.homes.title: Homes and Status
handbook.bettercoppers.homes.text:
Every working golem belongs to a copper chest, its home. It brings what it makes there and fetches its supplies from there.

# Linking
Sneak + right-click the golem with an empty hand, then right-click the copper chest. To move a golem, link it again.

# Changing your mind
Picking a golem changes nothing yet. It glows until you link it, cancel or half a minute is over. To cancel, right-click a golem with a job with an empty hand, or sneak + right-click a golem without a job again. Picking another golem cancels too.

# Status
The same sneak-click shows its job and home in the chat, and for every job except sorter and courier also its energy and rust. A plain click with an empty hand shows a working golem's status too, and changes nothing else. A golem without a job hands over what it holds, as usual.

# Seeing homes
While you sneak, copper particles run from every golem near you to its home. A golem with a job but no home puffs smoke.

# Staying close
With nothing to do, a golem with a home strolls about and walks back once it is more than 6 blocks from its chest.

# Ending a job
Sneak + right-click a golem twice with an empty hand, within 5 seconds. You get its tool or bundle, its plan and everything it carries; what does not fit lands at your feet. A chained cart unchains and stays where it is, still loaded. Home, eyes and trim stay with the golem.

# Changing jobs
Sneak + right-click it with a different job item. You get the old tool and everything it carries, and a chained cart stays chained. A new tool for the same job only swaps the tools.
handbook.bettercoppers.sorter.title: Sorter
handbook.bettercoppers.sorter.text:
Sneak + right-click a golem with a bundle. It keeps it in its off hand and empties its home chest, item by item.

# Where things go
1. a chest that already holds that item,
2. otherwise any barrel with room,
3. otherwise an empty chest.
It knows every container within 32 blocks (8 up and down).

# Item frames
Hang item frames on a chest or barrel to reserve it: it then takes only the items its frames show, and they go there before anywhere else.

One frame can stand for many items:
- A blast furnace: everything a blast furnace can smelt, such as ores and raw metals.
- A smoker: everything a smoker can cook, such as raw food.
- A furnace: everything a furnace can smelt. That includes cobblestone, sand and logs.
- A bundle: everything in the bundle. One of each item is enough.

To reserve a chest for furnaces or bundles themselves, put one in a bundle and frame that. An empty bundle lets nothing in.

# Quota Slips
A Quota Slip (paper and a copper ingot) says how much of each item a chest should hold. Hang it in a frame on the chest: golems then bring no more than that, and leave that much in it. It also counts as a frame showing those items.

To fill in a slip, either:
- sneak + right-click a chest or barrel that holds exactly what you want. An empty one clears the slip.
- right-click to open it, and click items from your inventory onto the grid. They stay yours. Left and right click add or remove one, shift + click 16. A slot holds up to one stack: for more, use another slot.

A sorter does not fetch anything. To refill a chest, send a courier to it.

# Working stock
A sorter shares its chest with another golem and leaves what that golem needs to do its job:
- spare tools of its job,
- a miner's torches, rails, planks and fences,
- 16 of every seed for a farmer, 8 of every sapling for a forester, 16 of every animal food, all shears, 4 buckets and 4 bowls for a keeper, 16 glass bottles for a beekeeper.
This also holds when the golems are linked to the two halves of a double chest.

It carries 16 items per trip. Now and then it opens a wrong chest first and shakes its head: that is just its character.

Sorters are free to run: no energy, no rust.
handbook.bettercoppers.cart.title: Copper Chest Minecart
handbook.bettercoppers.cart.text:
Craft a minecart with any copper chest. A golem towing one carries a whole cart load.

# Handing it over
Right-click the cart with an iron or copper chain so it follows you, then right-click a golem with an empty hand. Sneak + right-click the cart to unchain it. When the golem's job ends, the cart unchains and stays where it is, still loaded.

# Related items
A sorter loads everything related to the first item it picks up: stone also brings stone slabs, stairs and bricks, but not oak logs. Then it delivers everything in one trip.

Other jobs fill the cart before their own pouch.
handbook.bettercoppers.miner.title: Miner
handbook.bettercoppers.miner.text:
Miners dig a vanilla-style 3x3 mineshaft with plank floors, supports, torches and rails, a Staircase straight down, a Strip Mine, a wide Room and Pillar hall, or a Multilevel Mine of stacked tunnels.

# The plan
Craft a Survey Table: 2 paper over 2 copper ingots over 2 planks. Put paper in, choose a Mine Pattern (Mineshaft, Staircase, Strip Mine, Room and Pillar or Multilevel Mine) and a length (8 to 128, up to 64 for Room and Pillar) and take out the mineshaft plan.

Use the plan on the ground where the mine should start. The tunnel heads the way you look.

# Strip Mine
A 3x3 corridor with narrow branches to both sides every 3 blocks, to find as much ore as possible. Choose the branch length (4 to 32) at the table. It needs no rails, fences or supports, only torches if you want light.

# The golem
Sneak + right-click it with a copper pickaxe first, then with the plan: without a pickaxe in hand it refuses the plan. Then link it to a copper chest near the entrance.

# Supplies
In a mineshaft, without planks, fences and rails it does not dig. Keep those and torches in its chest; it fetches them when it needs them. Without torches it digs on and leaves them out.

# Staircase
A Staircase goes down one block for every block forward, one wide and 4 high so you can walk it too, with the plan's length as its depth. It stops above the bedrock. It takes no planks, fences or rails: only blocks to patch holes in the floor, and torches if you have them.

# On the job
It digs out ores touching what it digs and follows each vein for up to 16 ores, diamond, gold, redstone and emerald included. It plugs water and lava with filler it dug itself, such as cobblestone, stone or dirt, and walks home with up to 64 items. Link a sorter to the same chest to sort the loot.

Out of filler at water or lava, it gives up that part of the mine: the rest of a mineshaft's tunnel (it still lays its rails in the part it dug), the rest of a Staircase, one branch of a strip mine, or the rest of a strip mine's corridor. The plan and its status show where it gave up. Mark the plan again at the same spot to have that part dug: finished steps skip themselves.

Ending its job gives you the pickaxe and plan back. The plan keeps its progress.

# Room and Pillar
A wide hall, 3 high, 9 or 17 wide (the setting at the Survey Table), that starts right at the entrance. Every fourth row keeps pillars of rock standing, and every other row of pillars gets torches. It takes no rails, fences or planks; torches are optional.

Out of filler at water or lava, it gives up the outer part of that half-row and digs on. In the centre column it gives up the rest of the hall.

# Multilevel Mine
Mineshafts of the plan's length stacked straight down, 6 blocks apart: 2 to 8 levels (the setting at the Survey Table). Levels that would reach the bedrock are left out. Carved stairs join them just behind the entrance, turning off to the right, so keep that ground free. Each level takes planks, fences and rails like a mineshaft, and is finished, rails included, before the next. Every trip goes to the one chest at the top.

Out of filler at water or lava in a tunnel, it gives up the rest of that level, lays its rails in the part it dug and goes on to the next level. On the stairs it gives up everything below.

# Diamonds!
When it finds diamonds, it digs out the whole vein and then hurries home with its antenna blinking, to show you.
handbook.bettercoppers.farmer.title: Farmer
handbook.bettercoppers.farmer.text:
Sneak + right-click a golem with a copper hoe. Its field is everything within 8 blocks of its home chest.

- It harvests ripe wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, nether wart, pitcher crops and torchflowers on farmland and replants them right away.
- It picks pumpkins and melons and leaves the stems.
- It picks ripe cocoa and replants it, and takes sweet berries and glow berries and leaves the plant. You place those first.
- It cuts sugar cane, bamboo and cactus once they are 3 high.
- It picks mushrooms but leaves the last one of a patch, so it can spread again.
- It takes a chorus plant whole once no flower on it lives, then plants a new flower.

It keeps 16 of every seed it can plant. It never tills new land: you build the field, the golem looks after it. A stem needs a free block next to it for its fruit, so leave those spots as plain dirt. Sneak + right-click the farmer with seeds to give it some.
handbook.bettercoppers.workers.title: Forester, Fisher, Keeper, Beekeeper, Crafter
handbook.bettercoppers.workers.text:
Sneak + right-click a golem with one of these items to give it the job.

# Forester: a copper axe
Fells natural trees within 12 blocks, never logs you placed. It collects saplings, apples, sticks and logs and replants every stump, four for a tree with a 2x2 trunk. A stump only takes the species that grew there and stays empty until the golem has that sapling. The axe only works on a clean golem; a rusty one it scrapes instead.

# Fisher: a fishing rod
Casts its line into open water within 10 blocks and waits for the float to dip: a catch every 20 to 50 seconds, fish and junk but no treasure.

# Animal keeper: a brush
Feeds pairs of animals with food from its chest so they breed, up to 16 of each kind. With shears in its chest it also shears sheep and brings the wool home. With empty buckets it milks cows, goats and mooshrooms, each animal once every 5 minutes, and with bowls it gets stew from mooshrooms.

# Beekeeper: shears
Takes the honey from full bee nests and beehives within 10 blocks, but only from those smoked by a lit campfire below them, so the bees stay calm. With glass bottles from its chest it fills one bottle per hive, without them it shears three honeycomb. It does not climb, so keep the hives within its reach.

# Crafter: a crafting table
Crafts what the item frames on or next to its chest show, from the ingredients in that chest, until the chest holds a stack. A Quota Slip on the chest sets another amount, for example 16 Charging Pads.
handbook.bettercoppers.courier.title: Courier
handbook.bettercoppers.courier.text:
A courier carries everything from one chest to another, however far apart they are.

1. Sneak + right-click the golem with an empty hand.
2. Right-click a plain chest or barrel, or sneak + right-click a copper chest: it picks things up here. A plain click on a copper chest would make it its home.
3. Walk to the destination (you have 10 minutes) and right-click a chest, copper chest or barrel there.

It takes 16 items per trip, or a cart load with a chained cart. On the road it keeps the chunks around it loaded, so the route keeps working while you are far away. If the destination is full, it waits.

Hang item frames on the pickup chest and it takes only what they show, with the same rules as for a sorter. Other frames on the destination change nothing.

# Refilling a chest
Hang a Quota Slip on the destination and the courier keeps that chest filled. It waits there until something on the slip is running short, then fetches exactly that. What no longer fits goes back to the pickup chest. A Quota Slip on the pickup chest makes it leave that much behind.

This courier no longer empties the pickup chest, so a golem that has that chest as its home can end up with a full chest and stop.

A golem with a job takes no route, except a courier: give it a new route and it keeps what it carries and delivers it on the new route. Other jobs have to be ended first. Linking it to a home copper chest ends the route.
handbook.bettercoppers.travel.title: Minecarts and Boats
handbook.bettercoppers.travel.text:
A golem heading somewhere more than 24 blocks away looks around for a ride.

# Minecart
An empty minecart on straight rails that run the right way. The golem pushes it along at about four times walking speed and gets off near its goal.

# Boat
An empty boat on water that stretches the right way. The golem paddles straight towards its goal and climbs out at the shore.

A golem towing a cart always walks.
handbook.bettercoppers.danger.title: Monsters and Iron Golems
handbook.bettercoppers.danger.text:
Monsters hunt copper golems that have a job: zombies, skeletons, spiders, illagers and more. A copper golem has only 12 health.

# Guards
Iron golems stay near the copper golems with a job around them and attack any monster that hunts or hits one (except creepers).

# Repairs
When an iron golem nearby is badly hurt, a copper golem takes iron ingots from its home chest (or the nearest chest with iron) and repairs it: 25 health per ingot. A golem with only a home also uses iron ingots it already holds in its hand, and gives back what is left over.

So build an iron golem for every work site, and keep some iron in your chests.
handbook.bettercoppers.running_costs.tex:
Sorters and couriers are free. Every other job costs something.

# Energy
Work uses energy. At night, in a thunderstorm, or when it runs empty, the golem walks to a free Charging Pad near its home (3 copper ingots, lightning rod, redstone) and stands on it.

A steady signal does nothing: the pad charges on redstone pulses, so it needs a redstone clock. Every pulse gives a little energy; the faster the clock, the faster the charge, up to full in about 25 seconds. Build one pad per golem.

A golem that ran empty stays on the pad until it is full and does no work until then. If the pulses stop for 10 seconds, it goes back to work with the energy it has. A golem that only came for the night goes back to work in the morning.

# Sleeping
When you sleep through the night, every working golem with a free pad near its home wakes up fully charged, clock or not.

# Rust
Steady work makes a golem rust one stage every few days. Exposed golems work at 85% speed, weathered ones at 70%. Oxidized or waxed golems don't work at all, except as sorters and couriers.

# Scraping
Use an axe on the golem, or put an axe in a dispenser: every redstone pulse scrapes the golem in front of it by one stage.

# Tools
Job tools wear out and break.
handbook.bettercoppers.trims.title: Armour Trims
handbook.bettercoppers.trims.text:
Golems can wear armour trims, just for looks.

Sneak + right-click a golem with an armour trim smithing template, then with a trim material (iron, gold, copper, emerald, amethyst...). The material is used up; the template stays with the golem.

A new template or material changes the trim. Sneak + right-click with shears takes it off and gives the template back. If it wears a flower, the flower comes off first. With neither, shears make the golem a beekeeper.
handbook.bettercoppers.reference.title: Quick Reference
handbook.bettercoppers.reference.text:
# Job items
Bundle: sorter
Copper pickaxe + plan: miner
Copper hoe: farmer
Copper axe: forester
Fishing rod: fisher
Brush: animal keeper
Shears: beekeeper
Crafting table: crafter
Two chests: courier

# Clicks
Sneak + item on golem: hand it over
Sneak + empty hand on golem: status and linking
...then a copper chest: home
...then a chest, then another: courier route
...then sneak + copper chest, then a chest: the same
...again within 5 seconds: end its job
...again, no job: cancel
Empty hand on a golem with a job: status, cancel
Holding sneak: home lines

# Energy
Charging Pad + redstone clock

# Eyes
Iron / gold / diamond block: 1.5x / 2x / 3x radius

Lost this book? Craft a new one from a book and a copper ingot.

handbook.bettercoppers.tools.title: Tools and Eyes
handbook.bettercoppers.tools.text:
# Copper tools only
Golems work with copper pickaxes, axes and hoes, nothing fancier. Fishing rods, shears, brushes and crafting tables are fine as they are.

# Broken tools
When a tool breaks, the golem keeps its job. It brings home what it carries, then looks for the same tool in its home chest, and then in every chest and barrel within 16 blocks. So keep a few spare copper tools next to it. With none anywhere it waits and looks again every half minute.

To end its job instead, sneak + right-click it twice with an empty hand, within 5 seconds.

# Full or missing chest
A full chest costs you nothing: the golem keeps what does not fit and stops working. It leaves crops and ore where they are and waits at home until something it carries fits, then carries on by itself. Click it with an empty hand: its status says when the home chest is full. If the chest is broken or its chunk is not loaded, the golem stops working and waits with everything it carries, until the chest is back or you link a new one. Its items only drop if it dies or turns into a statue.

# Eyes
Sneak + right-click a golem with a block of iron, gold or diamond. Its eyes glow in that colour and it works further from home:
- Iron: 1.5 times the radius
- Gold: 2 times
- Diamond: 3 times
This widens fields, forests, fishing water, animal pens, the chests a sorter knows, how far a miner follows a vein and where an operator looks for spare parts. Couriers don't need it. A new block replaces the old one, and the block drops when the golem dies.

message.bettercoppers.eyes_courier: Couriers don't need sharper eyes: they go wherever their route leads.
